He knew who would betray him. He washed his feet anyway. 🍞 John 13

On the night before the cross, Jesus “riseth from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a towel” (John 13:4) and washed his disciples' feet, all of them. “For he knew who should betray him” (John 13:11). Then he took bread and said, “This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me” (Luke 22:19).

Who is God asking you to serve this week, even if it's hard? 👇

He called himself a dead dog. The king gave him a seat at his table. 👑 2 Samuel 9

Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, was lame on his feet since he was five (2 Samuel 4:4). When King David asked, “Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him?” (2 Samuel 9:3), he was brought in and fell on his face. David said, “Fear not,” and promised: “thou shalt eat bread at my table continually” (2 Samuel 9:7).

Have you ever felt too broken to be wanted by God? Type “GRACE” if this story speaks to you 👇

Don't let the holidays pause your faith. 🦃📖

5 ways to stay close to God over Thanksgiving and winter break: Bible before the group chat. Worship playlist on the long drive home. Say thank you out loud at the table. Quiet time, even on the couch. And one chapter a day, even on break. “In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you” (1 Thessalonians 5:18).

Which one is hardest for you over break? Comment 1 to 5 👇

His friends fell asleep on the hardest night of his life. 🌙 Matthew 26

In Gethsemane Jesus said, “My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death” (Matthew 26:38). He prayed, “nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt” (Matthew 26:39), and “his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground” (Luke 22:44). His disciples? Asleep. “Could ye not watch with me one hour?” (Matthew 26:40).

What's one thing you need to pray “not my will, but Yours” over? 👇

400 men with swords. One woman stood in the way. ⚔️ 1 Samuel 25

Nabal insulted David: “Who is David?” (1 Samuel 25:10). David told his men, “Gird ye on every man his sword” (1 Samuel 25:13). But Abigail “made haste” with bread, wine and food, fell before David, and stopped him. David said, “blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood” (1 Samuel 25:33).

Have you ever been stopped from a decision you'd regret? 👇
